judged_text: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist is lowercased at load time but compared against raw-case guest input via case-sensitive includes, so any case variation bypasses the blocklist. With BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='spam@evil.com', a caller submits 'SPAM@evil.com'; blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is false, the attendee row is created and invite emails are sent to the blacklisted address, defeating the abuse control the env var exists for.

With BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='spam@evil.com', a caller submits 'SPAM@evil.com'; blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) is false, the attendee row is created and invite emails are sent to the blacklisted address, defeating the abuse control the env var exists for.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses the raw `guest` input: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `includes` is case-sensitive and `guest` is not lowercased/normalized, a caller can bypass the blacklist by changing the email case (e.g., `SPAM@evil.com`). This would allow creating attendee rows and sending emails to a blocked address.
